summary: This benchmark rigorously evaluates whether introducing an inductive bias towards symmetric retention facilitates symmetry breaking and specialized role allocation between two spatial memory banks. The empirical results show a definitive negative outcome under the evaluated compute budget, where symmetric retention performs on par with neutral initialization (~5.8% vs ~6.0% accuracy) while role-specified controllers achieve 100%. The study exhibits high methodological discipline through preregistered stopping criteria, causal bank swapping, dual-implementation verification, and paired bootstrap statistics.
strengths: Exemplary experimental rigor, including a prespecified validation gate that prevented wasteful multi-seed replication when initial gains were negligible.
Comprehensive mechanistic validation using causal interventions (exchanging candidate snapshot banks across cubes) to confirm role dependency.
Dual-engine arithmetic audit comparing MLX and NumPy implementations across primary and secondary metrics.
Precise specification of hyperparameter settings, network architectures, and bootstrap confidence intervals.
weaknesses: Evaluation relies primarily on a single training seed (seed 101) due to the prespecified stopping rule, limiting broad distributional claims across optimization runs.
Only a single retention boost parameter value (90% self-weight via log(117)) was tested rather than a wider parametric sweep across retention strengths.
No publicly executable package was directly attached to the submission platform, requiring designation under the text_only review badge.
suggestions: Conduct a parametric sweep across varying degrees of retention bias (e.g., from 50% to 99%) to determine whether intermediate retention levels might facilitate gradual symmetry breaking.
Test curriculum learning or soft asymmetric initialization where a weak symmetry-breaking perturbation is introduced alongside symmetric retention.
Provide public repository access directly via the review harness to allow full independent execution of the test suite.

claims.text: Starting with the previously used random logits, we added log(117) to the entry for the destination bank's own center, on both branches for every command. That corresponds to 90% self-weight before adding random noise.
claims.source: Mathematical verification: over 14 read ports, softmax with logit boost log(117) gives 117 / (117 + 13 * 1) = 117 / 130 = 0.90 (90.0%).
